fun_highlights: The callback system genuinely earns its payoffs. When the child-who-looked-away (c_friend / looked_away) resurfaces decades later as cb_lookaway, or the hard-studied book from childhood closes as a circle in midlife (cb_books_late), the game briefly feels like literature rather than a card draw. In Dynasty 6, Ren re-reads the too-hard book at age 49 — the echo landing 38 years later is one of the few moments that felt irreplaceable. Coming back after weeks away, these callbacks are the first thing that makes me want to keep playing, because they prove the session remembers who I was.

The writing per-card is the game's strongest asset and holds up on return. Individual lines — 'felt the sense of it like a bruise' (turning the stray away), 'a quiet certainty for years now, Ronja is waiting for a question' (a_marry), 'the body has begun sending its small bills' (observe/vit_neg) — are specific enough that a lapsed player scanning the chronicle doesn't feel like they're reading a template. The prose tier is genuinely higher than the genre average.

The era system (war / plague / hard / plenty / turning / settled) creates real contextual variety at life-open. Dynasty 6 opens in war, Dynasty 11 in plague, Dynasty 15 in lean years — the calling card text, origin text, and marriage prompts all shift with the era, so a returning player sees the first two screens differently each time. The era's gate on cards like the war version of y_calling ('There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young') is one of the better structural differentiators.

The dynasty layer — motto, heirlooms, standing, collateral succession — is the most compelling return hook. Seeing 'Better a short blaze than a long smoke' or 'We do not save ourselves for later' crystallize mid-play, watching the house climb from a rented room to an old and famous house over five generations, is the game's strongest 'one more life' engine. The heirloom 'a book too hard for a child's hands' threading through House Salvedi across three generations (Ren, then Idris passing it on silently) is exactly the kind of dynastic texture the genre promises.

The competing-goods cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) are among the few beats where the choice itself resists easy reading — both options are articulated as real virtues. In a genre where most binary choices are transparent virtue-versus-vice, these cards make the player feel genuinely unsure, which is valuable. x_dream_or_duty ('both, she knows, are forms of love') is the best single prompt in the file.

The vocation-divergence structure (soldier / scholar / maker / wanderer / adrift) does produce meaningfully different lives in the transcript. A soldier life (Ren Salvedi) has the war card, the 'go where it's worst' fork, the PTSD callback; a scholar life (Naima Okonkwo, Cassian Ashby) has the study-pays callback, the knowledge-guard-vs-give decision, the final unanswered question. A lapsed player picking a vocation can anticipate a genuinely different shape, which makes the first choice feel meaningful.
staleness: The childhood sequence is a near-identical checklist across every single life: origin card → book-or-yard → sick-in-bed (or sibling) → lonely-child → unfairness. In the transcripts this recurs with striking fidelity: compare Carys Brandt (age 4 origin, 9 wonder, 17 stay-or-go, then c_unfair implied), Iris Brandt (age 6 unfair, 9 stray, 12 friend, 16 calling), Cassian Ashby (age 3 origin, 8 unfair, 12 book, 17 calling), and Naima Okonkwo (age 6 fever, 12 unfair, 19 calling). A returning player who has played five dynasties will recognise the opening 12 years as a predictable beat-sheet, which deflates the freshness of each new founder. The trait affinity boost in engine.js (bookish child leans c_book, restless leans c_move) is present but too weak to break the pattern — the trait-weight multiplier (2.6x) cannot overcome the fact that all these cards are nearly always eligible and low-cooldown simultaneously.

Body-age observations (the vit_tire and vit_neg pools in observe()) fire on every long-lived character and use the same ten-line pools across every life. Within a single session of fifteen dynasties, lines like 'the stairs have started to ask a question of them', 'mornings take longer to arrive in the body than they once did', and 'he has grown courteous with his own body, the way one is with the powerful' appear verbatim in multiple lives. Dynasty 8 Cyrus has 'he has started to plan the day around what the body will permit' (age 77); Dynasty 14 Niall has 'he has grown courteous with his own body' (age 79). The firedObs key prevents repeats within one life but the pools are shared across all lives, so a long session accumulates visible repetition. For a lapsed player this is the most visible staleness — scanning a new chronicle and immediately recognising the 'body bills' phrasing.

The marriage and child beats converge on a narrow band of phrasings that a returning player memorises quickly. 'Had a child, X, well past when they had thought that particular door had closed' appears or closely echoes across Dynasty 1 (Henrik, age 42), Dynasty 2 (Edmund, age 45), Dynasty 5 (Lazlo, implied), Dynasty 6 (Linnea, age 47), Dynasty 11 (Linnea again, age 47), Dynasty 12 (Ottilie, age 31). The engine comment in engine.js ('the old hard force at the window's end... clustered every birth into the late 40s') acknowledges the problem was fixed, but the latePool phrasing is still narrow enough that even the 'fixed' version reads the same. Similarly 'married X in front of the few who mattered, and let the world find out after' recurs for multiple wanderer-type characters (Anders Salvedi, Noor Ashby, Ottilie Quint) because the wanderer-marriage framing pools are small.

The 'guard-vs-give knowledge' decision (cb_study_pays: 'name your worth' vs 'teach it cheap') fires in a significant majority of scholar and teacher lives — visibly recurring across Dynasty 1 (Iris), Dynasty 2 (Tobias), Dynasty 4 (Ottilie Mercer), Dynasty 6 (Otto), Dynasty 8 (Cassian), Dynasty 9 (Anders Sereno), Dynasty 11 (Naima). The onceDyn cooldown is set to default (3 generations), but because it fires per-dynasty and the game runs many short single-gen dynasties, the rate of recurrence remains high across a session. A lapsed player will pre-answer it without reading it.

The epitaph pool produces visible clustering in the transcripts. 'Taught what they knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' appears verbatim for Linnea Okonkwo (D11 gen 2) and Lazlo Bjornsen (D5). 'Left people gentler than they found them' appears for both Anders Salvedi (D6 founder) and Noor Ashby (D8 founder). 'Kind in the small daily ways that turn out to be the large ones' appears for both Edmund Ashby (D2 gen 2) and Theda Quint (D12 gen 3). The dynasty.js epitaph logic has a per-dynasty dedup and a session-wide RECENT_LINES guard, but the combination of a short epitaph pool and fifteen dynasties is enough to produce these exact repeats. For a lapsed player, the death screen — which should feel like a capstone — often reads as familiar.

The 'reckoning' callbacks (cb_principle, cb_the_cost) and the body-health card (m_health) all converge on a predictable midlife structure: a decision made young is restated as a question, the player re-chooses, the game logs the echo. In the transcripts this produces a structural sameness across different lives — by the late adult years, a lapsed player recognises the 'here comes the reckoning' pattern and begins anticipating it rather than experiencing it. The onceDyn cooldowns for these cards are set to 5 generations, which should help across a very long dynasty, but in short dynasties (the majority in the transcripts) it still lands in most lives.

improvements.what: Expand and differentiate the childhood sequence by enforcing a per-session soft limit on how many of the core child cards can fire in consecutive lives, and by making two of the five standard childhood beats mutually exclusive per life (e.g. either c_friend OR c_unfair in the same life, not both).
improvements.why: The childhood checklist is the most immediately recognisable pattern for a returning player. Even if individual phrasings are fresh, the beat-order (origin, wonder/book, illness, social, unfairness) is predictable within the first three screen-cards. Making the early years genuinely structurally different — some lives never meet a lonely child, some never get the unfairness moment — would make the 'who is this person' question feel open again on return.

improvements.what: Substantially expand the body-age observation pools (vit_tire and vit_neg in engine.js observe()) from 10 lines each to 20-25 lines, with a session-level dedup that prevents any single phrasing from appearing more than twice across a full session's worth of lives.
improvements.why: These observations fire on every life that runs past 40, and they share pools across all lives in a session. They are the most verbatim-repeated text in the transcripts — a lapsed player scanning any chronicle will encounter familiar phrasing within the first page. The fix is low-effort (prose writing) and high-impact for perceived freshness.

improvements.what: Give the cb_study_pays and m_mentor_young cards an onceDyn cooldown of 5-6 (currently default 3 and no onceDyn respectively), and split cb_study_pays into two variants gated on whether the character taught or guarded knowledge earlier, so the callback reads differently depending on the established character.
improvements.why: The guard-vs-give knowledge fork is the most over-repeated mid-life decision in the transcripts, appearing in seven of fifteen dynasties. Raising the cooldown and splitting the text by prior choice would reduce frequency and make the instances that do fire feel earned rather than scheduled.

improvements.what: Expand the late-birth and marriage phrasing pools (latePool and the >48 marriage lines in a_marry and haveChild in engine.js) to include 4-5 additional lines, and add a session-level freshPick guard (like RECENT_LINES) specifically to these pools so a single session cannot repeat the same birth or marriage phrase.
improvements.why: The 'had a child, past when they thought that particular door had closed' phrasing and the wanderer-marriage framings are the second most visible verbatim repetitions in the transcripts, and they are concentrated in the emotionally significant moments (birth, marriage) where a player is most attentive to the prose.

improvements.what: Add two to three genuinely non-domestic adult-arc cards — events that fire for childless, unmarried, or solitary lives and give those lives distinctive texture rather than running on the same universal pool as domestic lives. Currently a solitary life (no spouse, no child) gets the same midlife and elder beats as any other, minus the domestic cards; the 'absence' is not named or explored.
improvements.why: The transcripts show that solitary lives (Junia Calloway, Calla Okonkwo, Anders Sereno, Theda Quint) are structurally identical to domestic lives with different relationship slots, not genuinely different in tone or content. A card that only fires for a life that reached midlife alone — exploring the particular textures of a life without heirs — would give solitary lives a reason to be played deliberately rather than merely accepted.

verdict: A Life has real craft in its callback system and vocation arcs, and individual card writing strong enough to hold a return visit. But coming back after time away, the childhood sequence reads as a memorised checklist and the shared observation pools produce visible verbatim repetition across lives — the body's 'quiet bills', the late child, the guarded-knowledge fork all arrive on schedule. The game passes 6 comfortably because the dynasty layer and the competing-goods cards generate genuine pull; it doesn't reach 7 because a lapsed player re-recognises the template within the first two lives of a session. The staleness is concentrated in addressable places (observation pool depth, childhood structure, a handful of over-fired callbacks), and fixing even two of them would meaningfully change the return experience.
